body: The new app's controls: each one an ordinary driver step on an actionable, named control whose handler panics, returns an error the root error boundary takes, or logs.

The actions answer and an acting call's answer on the new app: every `caused` item tied to the control's stable id, owner and event, with no new cause, verb, argument, carrier, session error, exit, node key, log field or span.

The new app's interactive nodes each carry an accessible name and are read as actionable by the one actionable rule, so the snapshot, the UI graph and the actions listing show them the way they show the six apps' controls.

The new app's screen at boot reads 0 lint findings and its text and controls meet the stand's SC 1.4.3 contrast thresholds, as the lean stand screens do; its snapshot stays under SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET.
The new app's expected roles, names and focus order stated once in the stand's shared expectation tables, read by its headless boot in both layout modes.

The authored error text, every panic message, Err text and log message and field the app writes, carries no field of the scrub's hidden set (url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, error, password, panic.payload), no host path, no secret and no user text, so the log sink's allowlist and redaction for escher's own targets leave it whole and it crosses in `caused` in full.
The served-task table grows by one entry; the six served apps' answers stay byte for byte as they are, held by their kept checks and the stand's cross-OS readings.
The new stand checks join the stand-repeat leg's three rounds by name and the blitz-tests target pin.

The stand binaries still build no platform adapter and the stand stays at accessibility tier 0 with the new app on it; the capability statement's reach is edited by hand where its served-app counts move.

The stand prompt's new goal, to meet the error page and make sense of what its controls cause, phrased once; the verdict's new count read from the live server child's kept checks or transcript as bools and counts only, never the text.
The P5 card says, per control, what an agent reads in `caused`.

Each new stand check is a named target of the stand-repeat leg, repeated three rounds, and gates CI.
A new stand screen's expected roles and names are stated once, in the stand's expectation tables, not repeated per test.

body: Range input rows, its keys, pointerdown, click and value: the new app's controls panic, return an error or log and are no range input.
Single-choice and multiple select rows, open and closed lists, optgroups, typeahead and their colours, row heights and motion: the error page opens no select list.
Cells grid and CRUD list keyboard contracts: those apps stay as they are.
Password value masking, caret and reveal rules: the new app has no password field.
Driver screenshot contracts, element and row shots: the chunk adds no screenshot behaviour.
Scrollbar thumb contrast, scrollbar drag, hidpi or zoom reshaping and scheme-change rows: the chunk changes no engine painting or viewport behaviour.
Engine ARIA property reads and role mapping rules (aria-describedby, aria-level, aria-expanded, HTML-AAM): the chunk changes no engine reading of the tree, it only adds a screen read by them.
Invalid date state rules: the new app carries no date field.

body: The new served app's controls, each reached by an ordinary driver step (an acting verb on a control), cause a handler panic, a handler `Err` taken by the root error boundary, and a handler log, so the acting call's answer carries `caused` items naming the control's stable id, owner and event.
The served-task table grows by exactly one entry; the new app is listed in the session status's served tasks and reached through the session host and the mcp role as the six other served tasks are.

The new app's stand checks boot it headlessly through the seven_guis headless stand, run in both layout modes, on the bundled font with no skip, and are witnessed inside stand-repeat at the zero-failure budget.
Indirect, through the engine's `caused` record class: engine caused items are asserted on a tracing build only, so the new checks of `caused` items stand where that build runs.

Indirect, through the root error boundary: a root-boundary `Err` is checked on its own session, so the control returning an error is driven on a session of its own apart from the panic and log controls.

Every authored panic message, `Err` text and log message and field the new app writes is the app's own fixed text, carrying no field of the scrub's hidden set, no host path, no secret and no user text, so what crosses in `caused` to the model provider is read in full; driver, stand and session log lines keep fixed words and counts only, with no ids or names.
Indirect, through agent-run and cold-agent outputs: a handler panic's text never reaches agent-run output or cold-agent events, which stay content-free.
The new app's snapshot stays within the snapshot text budget and its boot reads 0 lint findings, as the lean stand screens do.
The six existing served apps' answers stay byte for byte as they are, held by their kept checks and the cross-OS readings of the served tasks by answer digest.

No new driver verb, argument kind, run carrier, refusal cause, session error, exit code, snapshot node key, log field or span is added; the new app is reached through the existing verb table and acting verbs only.

The stand prompt gains a goal asking the cold agent to meet the error page and make sense of what its controls cause, phrased once (the prompt goal control pins a phrase standing once), naming no element ids or app slugs.

The cold-agent verdict gains a count of the calls whose answer carried `caused`, read from the live server child's kept checks or transcript as bools and counts only, never the text, and a field saying whether the run is required to meet it beside the pipe's other required counts; the run still passes only on positive evidence and an empty run is never a pass.
The cold-agent pipe's contract tests stay offline under unittest and pin the new prompt goal and verdict count; the live cold-agent run stays off CI and is not fired by this chunk.
The capability statement's served-app count and its pins move together, the claim section names and counts held to the schema, each claim naming its checks.
Indirect, through the stand's task state: the new app's state is registered for the UI graph and the shared graph drives exercise its writes as they do every stand write.
The new stand check file is a blitz-tests target of its own, joins the pinned target list and the stand-repeat leg's named targets, and keeps any leg it joins.
